processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Parent solution-treatment step preceding the 490°C aging; the material is a cast Fe-30Mn-9Al-1.56Si-0.9C-0.5Mo steel.
Age hardening at 490°C for 63 h used to compare κ-carbide size in 0.59% and 1.56% Si steels.

structures.overall_structure: Aged austenite matrix with nanoscale κ-carbide precipitates

phases_present.morphology: dark, uniformly textured matrix in dark-field TEM
nanoscale precipitates appearing as scattered bright dots and short bright clusters

precipitates.distribution: dense, numerous, and uniformly dispersed; greater size and number density than in the 0.59% Si steel aged identically

interfaces.phase_evolution: κ-carbide precipitation during aging; increasing silicon (0.59% to 1.56%) accelerates κ-carbide formation and increases its apparent size and number density.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI Tecnai F20 scanning/transmission electron microscope
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Aged 63 h at 490°C; dark-field imaging with a 10 nm scale bar
characterization_methods.purpose: Compare κ-carbide precipitate size and number density between 0.59% Si and 1.56% Si steels aged identically
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 1.56% Si steel shows denser, more numerous and more uniformly dispersed κ-carbide precipitates than the 0.59% Si steel.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: SAED pattern inset in dark-field TEM image (Fig. 3b)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Regular array of bright diffraction spots indicates crystalline κ-carbide; the spot arrays of the 0.59% and 1.56% Si specimens appear to be of the same type.
